journal-title-group.journal-title: Journal of Constructed Avian Cell Studies

title-group.article-title: Proliferation of primary duck hepatocytes under defined serum-free conditions

abstract.p: Primary hepatocytes isolated from Pekin duck (Anas platyrhynchos domesticus) were maintained in a defined serum-free medium. Cell number increased 3.1-fold over 96 hours. Proliferation was the only endpoint measured; lipid content was not assessed.

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Cultivated avian hepatic tissue is of interest for alternative foie gras production. A prerequisite is that avian hepatocytes can be expanded in culture. This study asks whether primary duck hepatocytes proliferate under defined serum-free conditions.

sec.title: Methods
sec.p: Hepatocytes were isolated from three Pekin ducks by two-step collagenase perfusion and seeded at 20,000 cells per square centimetre on collagen-coated plates. The medium was William's E supplemented with insulin, transferrin, selenium, dexamethasone and 20 ng/mL hepatocyte growth factor. Cell number was counted at 0, 48 and 96 hours by nuclear staining. Lipid accumulation was not measured in this study.

sec.title: Results
sec.p: Duck hepatocytes proliferated under the defined conditions. Cell number increased 3.1-fold between 0 and 96 hours (Table 1), with viability above 90 percent at every time point. Cells retained albumin secretion through 96 hours. No measurement of intracellular lipid was made.

caption.p: Cell number over time in defined serum-free medium

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: Primary duck hepatocytes can be expanded in a defined medium for at least four days. Whether these cells accumulate lipid under steatosis-inducing conditions was not tested and remains an open question.
